ZETA (Zero Energy Thermonuclear Assembly) was a major early fusion experiment. It was a toroidal pinch built at the UK Atomic Energy Research Establishment. ZETA was larger and more powerful than any fusion machine in the world until the mid 1960s. Its goal was to produce a measurable rate of fusion reactions, although it was not large enough to produce net energy.

It started operation in August 1957 and quickly detected neutrons, a by-product of fusion. The fuel temperature was believed to be 1-5 million degrees, enough for fusion. The result was leaked to the press in September 1957. It was reported worldwide as a greater scientific accomplishment than the Soviet Sputnik.

and Soviet experiments had detected similar neutron bursts at temperatures too low for fusion, justifying skepticism. Improved measurements found ZETA temperatures had been overestimated. The laboratory had to publicly clarify that ZETA had not achieved fusion, embarrassing the fusion research field. The neutrons were due to plasma instabilities that actually impeded steady state fusion.
